I will run the full 8 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is what fits my land, my well water, and my labor. I have farmed a long time, so I do not start from zero every year. I start from what worked last year and then trim or add a little based on weather, input price, and how the crop looked. For wheat, I will keep the stand steady and push for a stable ear count, so I will not save too much on base fertilizer. Wheat on my ground responds clearly to nitrogen, but if I push nitrogen alone and do not hold phosphorus and potassium, the crop looks strong early and then falls off later, so I will keep the three nutrients balanced. With well irrigation, I will plan on three waterings for wheat: one over winter if the soil is dry, one at jointing, and one at filling if needed. For maize, I will still put money into fertilizer because maize takes yield fast when water and fertilizer keep up together. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain yield. I will use hybrid maize seed, keep nitrogen a little lower than wasteful levels, and split it so the crop gets fed when it is growing fastest. On 8 mu, I can still manage it carefully with family labor, and because I have irrigation, I will not let the crop sit dry at the key stages. I will also keep pesticide sprays to the main problem windows instead of spraying blindly, because fertilizer, seed, pesticide, and irrigation all come from the same household budget.
